title: Integral logarithmic pullback at smooth and marked images
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$, fraction field $K$ and residue field $k$, and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ be projective flat finitely presented morphisms whose geometric fibres are nonempty connected reduced curves of pure dimension one with only ordinary double points. Give them pairwise disjoint sections $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ and $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ in the relative smooth loci, with $n\geq0$. The meanings of marked nodal family and of its canonically normalized dualizing invertible module are those of [lem-sfb-nodal-log-canonical-reconstruction]. Put $D_X=\sum_j a_j(S)$, $D_Y=\sum_j b_j(S)$ and $L_X=\omega_{X/R}(D_X)$, $L_Y=\omega_{Y/R}(D_Y)$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Let $p:Y\to X$ be an $S$-morphism with $p b_j=a_j$ and assume $p_K:Y_K\to X_K$ is an isomorphism. Let $M=(p^*L_X)^\vee\otimes L_Y$ [def-pc-module-pullback, def-sc-invertible-module], and let $s_K\in\Gamma(Y_K,M|_{Y_K})$ be the section corresponding to the canonical logarithmic-dualizing pullback isomorphism of $p_K$. For a generic point $\eta$ of an irreducible component of $Y_k$, set $A=\mathcal O_{Y,\eta}$ and regard the germ of $s_K$ as an element of $M_\eta[1/\pi]$; this is restriction to the inverse image of $Y_K$ in $\operatorname{Spec}A$. If $p(\eta)$ belongs to the relative smooth locus of $X/S$, then $s_K$ belongs to the image of $M_\eta\to M_\eta[1/\pi]$. This includes both unmarked and marked images of $\eta$, even if $p$ contracts its special-fibre component to a marked point. More explicitly, $\eta$ is relatively smooth and unmarked, $A$ is a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$, and $A[1/\pi]$ is its fraction field. For every nonzero $a\in A$ there are $m\geq0$ and $w\in A^\times$ with $a=\pi^m w$, and the relative logarithmic differential $\mathrm da/a$ in $\Omega^1_{A[1/\pi]/R}$ is the image of $w^{-1}\mathrm dw\in\Omega^1_{A/R}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. At a marked image, any centred etale coordinate $t$ with that section as zero scheme has logarithmic frame $\mathrm dt/t$; its pullback $p^*t$ is nonzero and the generic image of this frame is the regular differential just specified. No properness of $p$, normality of the total spaces, positivity, or smoothness of the whole generic fibre is assumed.

source.place: Tag 054L (lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space), centred smooth-section coordinates; agent logarithmic-integrality argument from old lem-sfb-nodal-log-dualizing-pullback Steps 2, 4 and 5, using algebra.tex lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module and duality.tex lemma-fundamental-class-lci. Not a verbatim assertion of the tag.

proof.text: Finite presentation over the Noetherian affine $S$ makes $Y$ locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft]; quasi-compactness makes it Noetherian. Apply [lem-trf-generic-fibre-points-smooth] to $Y/S$: flatness, finite presentation and geometrically reduced fibres are hypotheses. Thus $\eta$ has a relatively smooth open neighbourhood $W$. Its nonempty fibres are open parts of pure one-dimensional fibres. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-trait-curve-local-properties] to $W/S$: $A$ is a Noetherian regular local domain and $\dim A=1+\dim\mathcal O_{Y_k,\eta}=1$. Indeed the fibre local ring is localization at a minimal prime, whose spectrum has just that prime, hence dimension zero.

[lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient] identifies $A/\pi A$ with the fibre local ring. This ring is reduced because $Y_k$ is reduced, and its only prime is its maximal ideal because $\eta$ is a component generic point. That maximal ideal is its nilradical, hence zero. Thus $A/\pi A$ is a field and $\mathfrak m_A=\pi A$. Flatness over $R$ makes $\pi$ a non-zero-divisor, in particular $\pi\ne0$ in the domain $A$; the discrete valuation ring property is derived from the definition in step 3.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), condition (4); schemes.tex Tag 0HA1 (lemma-local-ring-fibre). Agent local calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] to the Noetherian local ring $A$, ideal $(\pi)=\mathfrak m_A$ and finite module $A$. For $a\ne0$ there is therefore a largest $m\ge0$ with $a\in\pi^mA$. Write $a=\pi^m w$; maximality says $w\notin\mathfrak m_A$, hence $w$ is a unit. Consequently a nonzero ideal $I$ equals $\pi^{m_0}A$, where $m_0$ is the least exponent of its nonzero elements. Thus the local domain $A$ has only principal ideals and nonzero maximal ideal $\pi A$, so it is a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$ by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Every nonzero denominator in $A$ is consequently invertible in $A[1/\pi]$, so this localization is its fraction field $F$. This also identifies the inverse image of the generic fibre in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $\operatorname{Spec}F$.

source.place: Tag 00IQ (lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module), part (2); agent extraction of the valuation factorization as in Tag 00PD.

proof.text: Use the universal relative derivation of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. For $a=\pi^m w$ the Leibniz rule and $\mathrm d\pi=0$ give $\mathrm da=\pi^m\mathrm dw$. In $\Omega^1_{F/R}$ we obtain $a^{-1}\mathrm da=w^{-1}\mathrm dw$. The right hand side is the image of the indicated element of $\Omega^1_{A/R}$; the map to $\Omega^1_{F/R}$ is induced by the derivation $A\to F\to\Omega^1_{F/R}$. This includes $m=0$, arbitrary residue characteristic and nonzero constant $a$.

No marking contains $\eta$. On the special fibre each section is a closed rational point: on affine charts its augmentation has quotient $k$, hence maximal kernel. Such a point cannot be generic in a pure one-dimensional fibre. The marking divisors and the canonical identification $\omega_{Y/R}|_{W}=\Omega^1_{W/R}$ are supplied by [lem-sfb-nodal-log-canonical-reconstruction]. At $\eta$, the marking twist is consequently canonically trivial and $(L_Y)_\eta=\Omega^1_{A/R}$. For the last equality use the affine-local sheaf description of [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]: extension of an $R$-derivation to a localization is uniquely $D(b/c)=c^{-1}D(b)-bc^{-2}D(c)$, which identifies the localized differential module with the stalk differential module.

source.place: Tag 0E9Z (lemma-fundamental-class-lci), smooth locus; moduli-curves.tex Tag 0E6R; morphisms.tex Tag 01UT (lemma-differentials-affine). Agent localization calculation.

proof.text: Put $x=p(\eta)$ and first suppose $x\notin D_X$. Near $x$ the marked twist is trivial and the canonical dualizing line is $\Omega^1_{X/R}$ by [lem-sfb-nodal-log-canonical-reconstruction]. Apply the map of [def-a1-relative-differentials-pullback-map] on this smooth neighbourhood and near $\eta$. It sends $1\otimes\mathrm df$ to $\mathrm d(p^*f)$ and is defined integrally. On the generic fibre it is the canonical comparison for the isomorphism $p_K$, by the isomorphism compatibility in [lem-sfb-locnoeth-lci-curve-adjunction-gluing]. Its germ therefore supplies the required element of $M_\eta$ in the unmarked-image case.

source.place: Tag 01UV (lemma-functoriality-differentials); duality.tex Tag 0E9Z (lemma-fundamental-class-lci). Agent smooth-locus comparison.

proof.text: Now suppose $x\in a_j(S)$. Restrict to the smooth locus of $X/S$, which contains the section, and use [lem-sc-smooth-section-affine-coordinates] with relative dimension one. It supplies a centred etale coordinate $t$ whose zero scheme is exactly this section; remove the other disjoint markings. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine], the chart algebra over $R[t]$ has vanishing relative differentials and first cotangent homology. Hence [lem-trf-formally-etale-differentials-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis] make $\mathrm dt$ a basis of its relative differentials. The canonical smooth dualizing identification and the definition of the Cartier twist then give the frame $e_X=\mathrm dt/t$ of $L_X$. The same conclusion holds for any centred etale coordinate with this zero scheme.

source.place: Tag 054L (lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space); etale.tex Tag 024T (proposition-properties-sections); algebra.tex Tags 0H93 (lemma-formally-etale-omega), 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring); centred chart as in existing cited node.

proof.text: Let $a=p^*t\in A$. It is nonzero. Otherwise the generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ would map into $a_j(K)$; the marked isomorphism $p_K$ identifies its inverse image with $b_j(K)$. Since $b_j(S)$ is the closed divisor supplied by [lem-sfb-nodal-log-canonical-reconstruction], its inverse image in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is closed and would contain the generic point of the domain $A$, hence also its closed point $\eta$. This contradicts step 5. By step 3 write $a=\pi^m w$. Under [def-a1-relative-differentials-pullback-map] the generic image of $e_X$ is $a^{-1}\mathrm da=w^{-1}\mathrm dw$ by step 4. The isomorphism compatibility of [lem-sfb-locnoeth-lci-curve-adjunction-gluing] identifies this differential with the specified canonical generic logarithmic comparison, rather than an arbitrary scalar multiple.

source.place: Tag 01UV (lemma-functoriality-differentials); duality.tex Tag 0E9Z; agent nonvanishing and marked-generic-frame calculation.

proof.text: In the marked-image case define the germ of a homomorphism $(p^*L_X)_\eta\to(L_Y)_\eta$ by $p^*e_X\mapsto w^{-1}\mathrm dw$. Step 5 makes its value integral, and step 8 proves that its localization is the prescribed generic homomorphism. A homomorphism from a free rank-one module $P$ to a rank-one module $Q$ is the element $e^\vee\otimes v$ of $P^\vee\otimes Q$ sending $e$ to $v$, directly from [def-sc-invertible-module]. This yields an element of $M_\eta$ mapping to the germ of $s_K$. Together with step 6 this proves the assertion. For $n=0$ only step 6 occurs; a contracted marked image merely permits $m>0$ in step 8 and causes no pole.
